summary: The cut in is clean and static, but the rock at about 102 s opens a dark void gap beside the door and lifts the wall off the floor, and the door seems to move separately from the wall.

faults.what: As the wall rocks, a black vertical gap opens along the door's right edge (visible 101.99 to 102.19). It shows the empty void behind the door and wall pieces. The door looks like a separate card sitting in front of the wall.
faults.fix: Put a backing plane or matching wall colour behind the door. Or parent the door to the wall and keep the rock rotation pivot shared so no gap opens.

faults.what: The wall panels and door lift off the floor and tilt. A bright green floor wedge shows under the right wall panel and the door's bottom edge floats above the floor (102.03 to 102.13). The base no longer sits on the ground.
faults.fix: Pivot the rock at the wall base, or extend the wall geometry below the floor so the base stays hidden.

faults.what: The rock starts abruptly. The door and wall go from still at 101.99 to a clearly tilted pose by 102.03 to 102.06, with no anticipation. It matches the measured frame-difference spike.
faults.fix: Add one or two frames of anticipation and ease into the rock. Then overshoot and settle, rather than snapping.
